title: UPS Transfer-to-Battery Frequency
dataSources: Proxmox node/VM metrics (`proxmox:metric`), Docker container stats (`docker:stats`), Synology/TrueNAS (`synology:disk`, `truenas:pool`), Raspberry Pi host metrics, UPS status via NUT (`nut:ups`), uptime probes (`uptime:probe`).
app: Proxmox / Docker / Portainer, Synology/TrueNAS, Raspberry Pi, and UPS (NUT) metrics via the Splunk Universal Forwarder, collectd/telegraf, and HEC.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=nut:ups
| bin _time span=1w
| stats count(eval(status!="OL")) as battery_events by ups_name _time
| where battery_events>3
| sort - battery_events
description: Counts how often the UPS had to leave normal line power, which helps distinguish a stable utility feed from a quietly flaky one.
value: Frequent battery transfers eat into UPS life and explain weird host behaviour; knowing the pattern helps decide whether the real problem is the power feed, not the server.
implementation: Forward NUT status changes into Splunk; review weekly transfer counts and correlate spikes with storms or local wiring issues.
visualization: Weekly chart of UPS battery-transfer events.
detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites

• **Splunk**: Splunk Enterprise ≥9.0 or Splunk Cloud — a single-instance home lab is fine. Create `index=personal` with 90–365 day retention (`indexes.conf`).
• **HEC token**: Settings → Data Inputs → HTTP Event Collector → New Token → index `personal`. Store the token in your connector's environment (never commit it to git).
• **Upstream product**: Personal HEC index — HTTP Event Collector token on index=personal.
• **Subcategory context**: Home Lab & Self-Hosting — typical feeds: Proxmox node/VM metrics (`proxmox:metric`), Docker container stats (`docker:stats`), Synology/TrueNAS (`synology:disk`, `truenas:pool`), Raspberry Pi host metrics, UPS status via NUT (`nut:ups`)..
• **Sourcetypes in this search**: `nut:ups`.
• **Network**: The connector host must reach both the vendor API/MQTT broker and your Splunk HEC port (8088/tcp).

## Step 1 — Configure data collection

Route **Personal HEC index** events into `index=personal` with `sourcetype=nut:ups`.

**Collection method:** HTTP Event Collector token on index=personal.

**Reference endpoint / path:** `POST https://<splunk>:8088/services/collector/event`.

**Suggested poll interval:** depends on upstream connector.

**Key fields to extract:** `sourcetype-specific — see search filters`.

**Typical connector stack:** Proxmox / Docker / Portainer, Synology/TrueNAS, Raspberry Pi, and UPS (NUT) metrics via the Splunk Universal Forwarder, collectd/telegraf, and HEC..

**Author notes:** Forward NUT status changes into Splunk; review weekly transfer counts and correlate spikes with storms or local wiring issues.


Example HEC payload shape:

```json
{"index": "personal", "sourcetype": "nut:ups", "event": { ... vendor fields ... }}
```

Verify ingestion with:

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=nut:ups earliest=-24h | head 20
```

## Step 2 — Create the search and alert

This search implements **UPS Transfer-to-Battery Frequency** over `personal` data (primarily `sourcetype=nut:ups`) across the full search range. It applies numeric thresholds on `battery_events` (> 3) after count — tune these constants to your household baseline.

**Fields this search depends on:** `_time`, `battery_events`, `ups_name`. Confirm each is populated before scheduling alerts.

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=nut:ups
| bin _time span=1w
| stats count(eval(status!="OL")) as battery_events by ups_name _time
| where battery_events>3
| sort - battery_events
```

## Step 3 — Validate

**(a) Compare to vendor UI:** Splunk Search → index=personal | stats count by sourcetype. Totals for the same day/week should match within connector lag (usually one poll interval).

**(b) Field presence:**

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=nut:ups earliest=-7d
| head 50
| table _time, battery_events, ups_name
```

Every column the detection uses should be non-null on recent rows.

**(c) Volume sanity:**

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=nut:ups earliest=-30d
| timechart span=1d count
```

Flatlines usually mean a broken token, expired OAuth refresh, or HEC URL change.

**(d) Threshold calibration:** Profile `battery_events` before alerting:

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=nut:ups earliest=-30d
| stats perc50(battery_events) AS p50 perc90(battery_events) AS p90 perc99(battery_events) AS p99 max(battery_events) AS hi
```

## Step 4 — Operationalize

Create a companion dashboard titled `UC-25.8.13: Personal evidence` with the following panel layout:

**Panel 1 — Weekly Chart Of Ups Battery-Transfer Events (the key fields):** Configure according to standard Splunk visualization patterns for this panel type.


Time picker defaults: set to last 30 days with named presets for 24h, 7d, 30d, 90d, and 1y — the auditor needs all five windows without retyping. Enable scheduled PDF export for the full dashboard on the regulation's reporting cadence.

## Step 5 — Troubleshooting

**Personal HEC index — no Personal HEC index events / missing fields:** If `nut:ups` stops updating, re-check HEC token, index `personal`, and firewall to port 8088. Search `index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd group=http_event_collector` for rejection reasons. Confirm the Personal HEC index connector script is still running (`systemctl status` or cron log).

**Personal HEC index — NULL values in extracted fields:** The Personal HEC index JSON export shape drifted — compare a raw event (`index=personal sourcetype=nut:ups | head 1 | spath`) against the field names in Step 2. Re-map in the connector before changing the SPL.

**Personal HEC index — API error / auth denied (401/403):** Refresh tokens expire on most consumer APIs — re-authorize the scripted input, update `passwords.conf` / env vars, and verify the vendor developer app is not in sandbox mode.

**Personal HEC index — endpoint timeout / HTTP 429 throttling:** Back off the poll interval in the connector; Personal HEC index APIs often cap requests per 15 minutes on free tiers.

**Bucket misalignment:** `span=1w` buckets on UTC by default — if your routine is local-time based, add `| eval _time=_time + (local_offset)` or use `@d` / `@w` snap.

**Stale dashboard:** Confirm the saved search `dispatch.earliest_time` covers enough history for your `1w` buckets.
